The correct value is −2431/50, so none of the three solutions is fully correct. Solution 1 is the closest, with the right magnitude and the wrong sign.

**Setup.** Let S = {2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, 56, 72}. Define g(k) = k²f(k) − 1, a degree-9 polynomial with roots at the 8 points of S. So g(k) = c(k − a)p(k), where p(k) = ∏_{s∈S}(k − s).

**Conditions at 0.**
- Since k²f(k) = g(k) + 1 is divisible by k², we need g(0) = −1 and g′(0) = 0.
- The logarithmic derivative gives p′(0)/p(0) = −Σ 1/(n(n+1)) = −8/9.
- The condition g′(0) = 0 reads p(0) − a·p′(0) = 0. Therefore 1 + (8/9)a = 0, so a = −9/8.
- The condition g(0) = −1 gives −c·a·p(0) = −1, so c·a·p(0) = 1. Hence c = −8/(9p(0)), which is negative.

**Evaluate at 90.**
- g(90) = c(90 + 9/8)p(90) = −(8/(9p(0)))·(729/8)·p(90) = −81·p(90)/p(0).
- p(0) = 8!·9!.
- Since 90 − n(n+1) = (9 − n)(n + 10), p(90) = 8!·18!/10!.
- So p(90)/p(0) = 18!/(9!·10!) = 4862.
- Therefore g(90) = −81·4862 = −393822.

**Result.** f(90) − 1/90² = g(90)/8100 = −393822/8100 = −2431/50.

**Check on the other solutions.**
- Solution 1 follows the same method, but it loses the negative sign on c and reports +2431/50. Its magnitude is correct.
- Solution 2 uses r = +9/8 instead of −9/8 and makes further errors, giving 192049/4050.
- Solution 3 makes an unjustified claim about the leading coefficient and gets 0.
